about: Settings for the Risk Navigator (scripts/risk.py). Scores run 0-10 from a buyer's point of view: price risk is the risk of prices rising or swinging hard; supply risk is the risk of not getting material on time or on normal terms. Change weights or concentration figures here, never in the page.

materials.name: Lithium carbonate

conc.what: China makes about 70% of the world's lithium chemicals (IEA, 2024)
conc.source: IEA Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2025, via Mercom

assumptions: Price history is the Guangzhou Futures Exchange lithium carbonate main contract (daily close since July 2023), converted to US$ at each day's ECB exchange rate. When the exchange moves to the next contract month the series can jump slightly.
Forecasts are the average of the bank and broker forecasts tracked on the Raw materials page, each taken at the middle of its range.

materials.name: LFP cathode

conc.what: China makes about 98% of the world's LFP cathode (IEA, 2024)
conc.source: IEA Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2025, via Mercom

assumptions: There is no free daily LFP cathode price. Its trend and swings are worked out from the lithium price, using the site's cost model: about 0.24 t of lithium carbonate per tonne of cathode, plus iron phosphate and processing held at today's values, then scaled to SMM's latest cathode price.
This assumes iron phosphate and processing fees move much less than lithium, which held through 2025-26 (iron phosphate rose about 8% from July to October 2026 while lithium swung far more).

materials.name: Graphite anode

conc.what: China makes over 95% of the world's battery-grade graphite (IEA, 2024)
conc.source: IEA Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2025, via Mercom

assumptions: There is no free regular graphite anode price, so the two price drivers are assumptions, marked as such: the trend is set slightly above flat because SMM's October headlines describe artificial graphite anode as slightly raised and its raw materials as 'more likely to rise than fall' (headlines only; the articles could not be opened), and swings are set low because anode prices have moved little since early 2026.
China's export controls on artificial graphite anode, paused until 10 Nov 2026, would add licence costs and delays for buyers outside China; that date is counted as a price and supply risk.

momentum.detail: Assumed slightly rising: SMM headlines in October describe artificial graphite anode as slightly raised before the 1–8 Oct holiday and stable after, and its raw materials as 'more likely to rise than fall' (headlines only, not verified)

volatility.detail: Assumed low (about 10% a year): the anode price used on this site has not changed since Feb 2026 and SMM's weekly reviews mostly report stable prices

materials.name: Storage cell (314 Ah LFP)

conc.what: China makes about 80% of the world's battery cells (IEA, 2024); India's own cell making is still small
conc.source: IEA Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2025, via Mercom

assumptions: Price history is InfoLink's weekly 314 Ah storage cell average (China, excluding VAT).
The cost to make comes from the site's cell cost model (SMM-based quantities and today's material prices).

materials.name: EV cell (230 / 324 Ah LFP)

conc.what: China makes about 80% of the world's battery cells (IEA, 2024); India's own cell making is still small
conc.source: IEA Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2025, via Mercom

assumptions: TrendForce publishes the EV cell price only every few months in its free reports, so the recent trend uses TrendForce's latest reported move plus the storage cell's 3-month trend, and swings are assumed to match storage cells (same LFP chemistry, largely the same makers).
The cost to make uses the storage cell cost model; EV cells cost a little more to make, so the real margin is thinner than shown.

materials.name: Copper

conc.what: China refines over 40% of the world's copper (IEA, 2024); India also refines its own
conc.source: IEA Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2025, via Mercom

assumptions: Price history is the LME cash settlement price, daily since 2018 (via Westmetall).

materials.name: Aluminium

conc.what: China made 44.2 of the world's 73.8 million tonnes of primary aluminium in 2025 (60%); India is a large producer too

assumptions: Price history is the LME cash settlement price, daily since 2018 (via Westmetall).

Back-test warning: for aluminium, a high trend-and-swings score has not been followed by rises (since 2018 prices more often fell afterwards), so read its price score as a sign of possible swings, not of rising prices.

High: Consider fixing prices for the next order window, or index-linked contracts with a cap
Check the cost floor: if the price is close to the cost to make, there is little room left to fall
Review open quotes and their validity dates before they lapse
Elevated: Watch weekly and have an order ready to place
Prefer index-linked pricing over long fixed-price deals until direction is clear
Low: Spot or index-linked buying is reasonable
A good time to negotiate longer agreements if prices are near the cost floor

High: Confirm allocations and shipping dates with each supplier in writing
Check second-source qualification and safety stock for critical lines
Track export-licence and customs news daily
Elevated: Ask suppliers about export-licence exposure and lead times
Keep a qualified alternative ready for the most critical parts
Low: Normal ordering; keep watching the dates ahead

duties.text: Standard basic customs duty on lithium-ion accumulators (tariff item 8507 60 00) is 20%.

Stationary, grid-scale and industrial battery storage systems qualify for a concessional 10% (Notification 45/2025-Customs, S. No. 325); battery packs for making electric vehicles are excluded from that concession.
duties.source: CBIC Circular 45/2026-Customs, via TaxGuru; Mercom, 12 Oct 2026

duties.text: On top of basic duty: social welfare surcharge of 10% of the duty, and 18% IGST (normally reclaimable as input credit).

Union Budget 2026-27 extended nil duty on capital goods for making lithium-ion cells. The duty on cells imported to build EV packs could not be confirmed from a public source; check the current notification before using a figure.

capacity.text: India has about 86 GWh of battery manufacturing capacity, but 92% of it is pack or container assembly and only about 8% (roughly 7 GWh) is cell making, much of it still being built.
Under the ₹18,100-crore ACC PLI scheme only Ola runs cell capacity so far (2.5 of its planned 20 GWh), no maker has yet been paid an incentive, and cell imports keep rising.
